2153.sol: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence called as repetitive DNA, because in these sequences, a small stretch of DNA is repeated many times. 123150.sol: Brassica (mustard) belongs to family Brassicaceae. Family brassicaceae is characterised by polypetalous 4 petals, polysepalous 4 sepals, six stamens (which are in tetradynamous condition i.e. 4 +2 or in two whorls, 4 inner long and 2 outer short). Gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous unilocular with parietal placentation. Fruit is usually siliqua (dry dehiscent fruit formed by bicarpellary syncarpous gynoecium with replum) and rarely lomentum.

124734.sol: In plants, living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed dedifferentiation. The formation of secondary meristems like interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells are classic examples of dedifferentiation in natural plant growth. 125447.subject: Botany
125447.text: What is the role of thick walls in the bundle sheath cells of C4 plants?
options: To be impervious to gaseous exchange
125447.sol: The particularly large cells around the vascular bundles of the C4 plants are called bundle sheath cells, and the leaves which have such anatomy are said to have ‘Kranz’ anatomy. ‘Kranz’ means ‘wreath’ and is a reflection of the arrangement of cells. The bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles; they are characterised by having a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces.

125974.subject: Botany
125974.text: Which type of fruit develops without fertilization?
125974.sol: In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral parts degenerate and fall off. However, in a few species such as apple, strawberry, cashew, etc., the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation. Such fruits are called false fruits (Figure 1.15b). Most fruits however develop only from the ovary and are called true fruits. 126297.sol: In angiosperms, post-fertilization changes lead to the formation of seeds and fruits. Non-albuminous seeds completely consume the endosperm during embryo development. Groundnut is an example of a non-albuminous seed. Albuminous seeds retain a part of the endosperm as it is not completely used up. Castor is an example of an albuminous seed. 126552.sol: The sequence of amino acids i.e the positional information in a protein – which is the first amino acid, which is second, and so on – is called the primary structure (Figure 9.3 a) of a protein. A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by the first amino acid and the right end represented by the last amino acid. The first amino acid is also called N-terminal amino acid. The last amino acid is called the C-terminal amino acid. A protein thread does not exist throughout as an extended rigid rod.

126821.sol: Proteins are made up of polypeptides and the polypeptides are made up of amino acids linked by the peptide bonds. The glycosidic linkages are seen in the carbohydrates, the glucose units are linked by these linkages to form disaccharides and polysaccharides. The nucleotides are linked by the phosphodiester linkages and the unsaturated fatty acids are characterised by the C = C double bonds.

The phage genome is integrated into DNA of its bacterial host and may be replicated along with the host DNA, as in the case or bacteriophage lamda or may be maintained as extra chromosomal DNA, as in the case for bacteriophage, lambda P₁ .

127660.subject: Botany
127660.text: The first trophic level for the pyramid is taken by
127660.sol: This relationship is expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. The base of each pyramid represents the producers or the first trophic level while the apex represents tertiary or top level consumer. The three types of ecological pyramids that are usually studied are (a) pyramid of number; (b) pyramid of biomass and (c) pyramid of energy.

127984.subject: Zoology
127984.text: How are the rest of the sense organs in frogs, apart from eyes and internal ears, described?
127984.sol: Frog has different types of sense organs, namely organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ears). Out of these, eyes and internal ears are well-organised structures and the rest are cellular aggregations around nerve endings. Eyes in a frog are a pair of spherical structures situated in the orbit in skull. These are simple eyes (possessing only one unit). External ear is absent in frogs and only tympanum can be seen externally

128457.sol: Iodine is necessary for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid. Deficiency of iodine in our diet results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.

Thyroid Gland: Composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea. Thymus Gland: Lobular structure located between the lungs, behind the sternum, on the ventral side of the aorta.

128988.subject: Zoology
128988.text: Heart Valve Location A. Tricuspid Valve 1. At the opening of the pulmonary artery B. Bicuspid Valve 2. Between right atrium and right ventricle C. Pulmonary Valve 3. Between left atrium and left ventricle D. Aortic Valve 4. At the opening of the aorta
128988.sol: Tricuspid Valve is located between the right atrium and right ventricle, preventing the backflow of blood into the atrium during ventricular contraction. Bicuspid Valve (Mitral Valve) is situated between the left atrium and left ventricle, allowing blood to flow from the atrium to the ventricle without regurgitation. Pulmonary Valve is positioned at the opening of the pulmonary artery, controlling the flow of deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Aortic Valve is found at the opening of the aorta

130487.sol: The vertebral column in an adult human is differentiated into several regions starting from the skull. The distribution of vertebrae is as follows: Cervical: 7 vertebrae (A-III) Thoracic: 12 vertebrae (B-IV) Lumbar: 5 vertebrae (C-II) Sacral: 1 vertebra, which is formed by the fusion of 5 embryonic vertebrae (D-I) Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I. 130584.subject: Zoology
130584.text: How can progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen be administered to females besides oral pills?
options: As injections or implants under the skin
130584.sol: Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can also be used by females as injections or implants under the skin. Their mode of action is similar to that of pills and their effective periods are much longer. Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives as they could be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

130744.sol: According to NCERT, except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other sexually transmitted infections are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. From the given list, the incurable diseases are Genital herpes, Hepatitis-B, and HIV infection (3 diseases). The completely curable diseases are Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Chlamydiasis, Genital warts, and Trichomoniasis (5 diseases). Therefore, 5 of the listed diseases are completely curable. Answer: 5

133823.subject: Zoology
133823.text: What is the main advantage of using biofertilisers in agriculture?
options: It reduces dependence on chemical fertilisers
133823.sol: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the soil's nutrient quality and reduce the dependence on chemical fertilisers, thus reducing environmental pollution. The nodules on the roots of leguminous plants formed by the symbiotic association of Rhizobium. These bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms, which is used by the plant as nutrient. Other bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil (examples Azospirillum and Azotobacter), thus enriching thenitrogen content of the soil.

133919.sol: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in legume root nodules. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium in soil. Glomus forms mycorrhizal associations with plants. Anabaena is a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium.
